finding.summary: A resumable upload session lives on the cell container disk: a cell restart (rollout, crash, sleep) answers 404 no such upload, so the upload restarts from part 0. No data is lost or wrongly accepted — the desktop re-creates the session (creation is idempotent) and sends every part again — but S12 resume-verified-bytes does not hold on cloud.
finding.needsDecision: persist parts beyond the container (R2 multipart / DO storage) or accept restart-from-zero on cloud

S02.note: Control-plane invite rows (expired, revoked, viewer forged invite) were verified on 2026-09-22 against the same, unchanged control worker (followup-2026-09-22-cloud-auth.json). A removed designer's already-open cell session keeps working until the cell's revocation sweep — the product states this on the removal page ("stops working within the hour"); measured 121 s; writes in that window are allowed by design. Same-named projects on different servers: covered by self-host S02.

notInjectable.A-two-coordinators: one ProjectStore Durable Object per project; the platform runs one instance per id and serializes it — the cloud form is two people racing through the one cell plus the cell killed mid-burst (measured above)
notInjectable.B-missing-payload: payloads live in the DO storage; a test cannot delete one without corrupting the platform object
notInjectable.C-full-store: the DO storage cannot be filled for one test without breaking the cell

previousRuns.finding: D: parity mismatch ui-t32-probe (checkout) that survived two cell restarts — the cell studio held the canvas as body-rejected/local-edit on every wake: the checkout restored from the newest backup held an OLDER accepted version with no recorded base. Fixed 58b27496 (r9); after the r9 wake parity 115/115 with no cell-studio conflict, before any test write.

A oracle wrong: one coordinator merges a same-base race character-wise (19/20 rounds both win, 6 noop acks) — verified against the hub mergeLane; oracle now checks every head against an independent merge and excludes noop acks from the row check. The first burst finished before the kill; now 40 steps, kill at 700 ms (step 2 in flight).

starvedEdits.cause: A's proposal POST timed out at 20 s and was retried ('not acknowledged yet (The operation timed out.)'): the standard-1 cell (1/2 vCPU) was moving ~10 GB at once — A pulling the 2.6 GB this shared test project accumulated over earlier runs and uploading 0.64 GB, B and C each pulling ~3.2 GB
oracle artefact: B and C received the edit in 11 s through the hub; only the hub-head poll missed it

final.note: The load is ~3x the scenario design because the delete breaker (25/h) leaves earlier runs' files on the shared project; a fair re-measure needs a fresh test project.

S17.runner: runners/f3/s17-migration.mjs (cloud: relink after the cell restart, hub copy read through a socket)
S17.failingCause: The switch is interrupted by a HARD kill of the cell (destroy = SIGKILL). In legacy mode a cell's documents are only as durable as the last backup generation, so the legacy writes of the last minutes were gone after the restart (measured directly: documents written 5 s and 70 s before a hard kill, both lost). The desktop re-supplied them as new actions (desktopConverged true), so dryRun/bytesConserved/pendingWork fail on attribution, not on lost bytes on the desktop. forwardAgain answered 503 (platform request limit) while the switch completed.
S17.ownerDecision: 2026-09-24: narrow the window now (final backup on SIGTERM) and document the hard-kill residual -> 36e48e90
S17.importHangObserved: once: after a 503 on the switch, importPending stayed true >5 min with the revision not moving; a cell restart resumed and finished it at once. Cause not found (no container log access); runbook documents the recovery.
S17.regressionTests: 9a11e85a (rollback after an accepted-mode create; offline start with an unproposed save)
S17.ownerAcceptance: 2026-09-24: owner accepted S17 on the cloud with the documented hard-kill legacy residual (runbook) after 36e48e90 closed the graceful-stop window
